The Ohio Department of Education and Workforce (DEW), formally called the Ohio Department of Education, has shared with public schools across the state Senate Bill 288. This legislation requires that health education curricula be updated to include (K-12/developmentally appropriate) prevention education information in the areas of sexual abuse and sexual violence for students in public schools.As promised, the district is providing an opportunity for families to review the curriculum, and parents may opt their students out of the lessons if they choose.  For more information from the Ohio Department of Education- Click HERE. Instruction occurs annually. This year the district will conduct these updates with students October 12-26, 2026.K-3 Curriculum- Click HERE4-6 Curriculum- Click HERE7-8 Curriculum- TMSSocial Inclusion: Click HEREDating Violence: Click HERESuicide Prevention: Click HERE9-12 Curriculum - THS will share their videos in three successive weeks. Social Inclusion: Click HEREDating Violence / Healthy Relationships: Click HERESuicide Prevention: Click HEREContact your student's building and school counselor with any questions.

Instruction will occur **October 12-26, 2026** at Talawanda. Parents may **review curricula online** and opt students out if desired. Contact your student's school counselor with questions. Curriculum links are provided for all grade levels.

title: Reading Corner Title I Program Information
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Kramer 

Title 

Talk Kramer Title Talk

Reading Corner September NewsletterWhat is Reading Corner (Title I Reading)? We would like to take this opportunity to introduce you to our Title I Reading Corner Classroom! This is an opportunity for students to receive small-group reading instruction. The Title instructors, Mrs. Geshan, Mrs. Kobermann, and Mrs. Walters, will be working with qualified students for 30 minutes daily to enhance their literacy skills. We will work on targeted reading activities, such as letter naming, phonemic awareness, phonics, vocabulary, fluency, and comprehension.At the beginning of the school year and again in December, every student in grades K-3 is given a series of assessments used to help pinpoint students who may need a boost to help them become a successful reader. Using this data, students qualify for targeted small group reading instruction. We help students learn letter names and sounds, phonics patterns, oral reading fluency, as well as reading comprehension. Your child may simply need a beginning of the year boost in skills or they may remain in our care for the entire year. Students will be released from Title I Reading when they consistently meet the grade level benchmark. You are welcome to contact us at any time if you have any questions or concerns regarding your child’s progress in Reading Corner. geshanc@talawanda.org, kobermanc@talawanda.org or waltersh@talawanda.org

summary: **Reading Corner** is Kramer's Title I Reading program that provides small-group reading instruction to K-3 students who need extra literacy support. Students receive **30 minutes of daily instruction** from Mrs. Geshan, Mrs. Kobermann, and Mrs. Walters, focusing on letter naming, phonemic awareness, phonics, vocabulary, fluency, and comprehension. All K-3 students are assessed at the beginning of the year and again in **December** to determine eligibility, and students are released when they consistently meet grade-level benchmarks. Contact instructors at geshanc@talawanda.org, kobermanc@talawanda.org, or waltersh@talawanda.org with questions.

title: New Peachjar Digital Flyer System Launched
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Peachjar Peachjar

We are excited to announce a new partnership aimed at improving how we share information with you. Talawanda School District is launching Peachjar this 2026-2027 school year! Peachjar is an innovative digital flyer management system. It transitions our schools from paper handouts to electronic flyer delivery, and assists with ADA compliance to meet the new Ohio law mandates in this area.Why Are We Making the Switch?Eco-Friendly: Saves thousands of sheets of paper annually.Highly Convenient: Delivers school and community resources straight to your inbox.Accessible: View important updates anytime on your phone or computer.Saves Time: Frees up valuable administrative and classroom instruction time.What to Expect as a Parent/Community Member:You do not need to take any action to register. If your email address is on file with the district, Peachjar will automatically create an account for you.You will receive a weekly digest email containing school-approved flyers.You can view flyers by clicking the Peachjar button on our school website.Your email address is kept entirely confidential and is never shared.You can opt out or adjust your email frequency at any time.

summary: Talawanda School District is launching **Peachjar**, a digital flyer management system for the 2026-2027 school year that replaces paper handouts with electronic delivery. Parents automatically receive a **weekly digest email** of school-approved flyers if their email is on file—no registration needed. Flyers can also be viewed via the Peachjar button on the school website, and parents can opt out or adjust email frequency at any time.

title: Volunteer and Visitor Policy Requirements
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Volunteer 

& 

Visitor 

Policy Volunteer & Visitor Policy

As we continue with our volunteer policy this year, please remember that any adult volunteer who wishes to enter the school building must have a volunteer application on file with the office every school year. After a parent’s second visit to the building, or if they plan to chaperone, assist with a field trip, they are required to complete fingerprinting and a background check through the Central Registration Office. Please plan to complete this process at least 3 weeks prior to the event. This allows adequate time for the background check to be completed and for the appropriate information to be provided to the school administrator for planning purposes. Once completed, your background check is valid for 5 years.Central Registration Office:Ruth Michael📞 513-273-3101We appreciate your understanding and cooperation as we work to keep our students, staff, and school community safe. Public schools have implemented these regulations to comply with state and federal safety requirements regarding volunteers and visitors in schools.Thank you for helping us make safety a priority at Kramer Elementary! ❤️

summary: All adult volunteers must have a volunteer application on file each school year. After a second visit or before chaperoning/assisting with field trips, volunteers must complete **fingerprinting and background check** through the Central Registration Office at least **3 weeks prior** to the event. Background checks are valid for 5 years. Contact **Ruth Michael at 513-273-3101** for Central Registration.
